title: A Baby Turkey, a Feather Duster Mom, and a Best Friend
summary: It sounds like a story from a Disney movie, but it really happened. At the Raven Ridge Wildlife Center in Pennsylvania, a baby turkey and a mourning dove became best friends. Last spring, the center took in two orphaned turkey chicks. Workers gave them a feather duster to stand in for a mother turkey. Sadly, one chick did not survive. The center never raises a baby animal alone, so workers paired the chick that was left with a baby mourning dove of about the same size. Workers hoped they would comfort each other. It worked better than anyone expected. Months later, workers let the dove leave when it wanted. But the dove kept coming back to the turkey's cage. The center said keeping them caged for life just because they were cute would not be fair to wild animals. So it planned a joint release with a large sanctuary, letting the pair choose to stay together or go their own ways. After the release, the dove flew into the trees and the turkey started looking for food.
why_it_matters: It shows that friendship and kindness can help someone feel safe when they are lonely or far from home.

background_read: A wildlife center is a place that cares for hurt or orphaned wild animals until they can live on their own.
Baby animals need warmth and company to feel safe, so workers sometimes give them a soft object to cuddle or pair them with another young animal.
When the animals are ready, workers release them back into nature so they can live as wild animals.

WHAT: The two young birds became best friends, were cared for together, and were later released together.
